# Used in: the first user message of the chairman’s session (task phase), for every training, held-out-gate and final-evaluation session. Teammates do not receive it directly; the chairman forwards work via send_message.
YOUR FINAL ANSWER should be a number OR as few words as possible OR a comma separated list of numbers and/or strings.
- If asked for a number: don’t use comma to write your number, don’t use units such as $ or percent sign unless specified otherwise.
- If asked for a string: don’t use articles, don’t use abbreviations (e.g. for cities), write digits in plain text unless specified otherwise.
- Example: respond with ’Saint Louis’ instead of ’St. Louis’; respond with ’17’ instead of ’17m’.
State your final answer clearly as: "FINAL ANSWER: <your answer>"
# Scoring: text after the first "final answer:" (case-insensitive) in the chairman’s
# finalize_task output, lower-cased and stripped of non-alphanumerics, must equal the
# equally normalized reference answer. Self-contained GAIA subset only (no attached files);
# each task gets an empty scratch workspace for computation.
The following source code files are available in your workspace under `context/`:
- ... and {n - 50} more files (only if more than 50 files)
Write your solution code files into the `solution/` directory using `write_file`
working {language} code files that address all requirements.
**IMPORTANT**: You MUST write at least one file to `solution/` before finishing.
# Scoring: static-analysis LCBS score of the files in solution/; success iff LCBS >= 3.0 (of 5).
# LoCoBench has no FINAL ANSWER instruction (the output graded is the solution/ directory).
# Sent to every agent before each LLM call as a trailing user message that is not
# stored in the conversation (so the system-prompt prefix stays cache-stable).
# The step line is always present; the team-message line only for the chairman;
[Budget status -- automatic, not a message from a teammate]
{label}: "for the task" (task phase) | "in this phase" (L1/L2/L3 reflection)
If time runs out before the task is finalized, the task is scored as failed -- work done so far is not graded.
When this phase’s time runs out, it ends for everyone and the session moves to the next phase; anything not yet finalized is not carried over.
When this phase’s time runs out, the session ends; anything not yet finalized is not carried over.
# [Time: 12m 05s of 15m 00s remaining for the task] If time runs out before the task is finalized, the task is scored as failed -- work done so far is not graded.
